### Important Python File Summaries:

**cum\_vol\_finalversion.py:** takes in retrospective csv, outputs a spaghetti-style graph of cumulative volume, with the median, 25/75 percentile, and driest/wettest years highlighted- \*not by water year\* (purpose: 

**general\_forecast.py:** takes in retrospective CSV, plots first 9 months of observed, then median of next three months, along with a shaded 25/75 percentile and the wettest and driest, to give a nice statistical envelope \*not by water year\*

**median\_metrics\_baseline.py:** takes in retrospective data and does the LOYO loop: plots 9 months of observed data until the reference point, then the metrics are computed for each year (RMSE, NSE, Percent Error, etc.) 

**Stretch\_scale\_metrics.py:** takes in retrospective data and does LOYO loop, this time plots 9 months of observed data until the ref point, and then a stretched/scaled forecast. The stretch is based on when the river got to 0.5 median volume, and the scaling is based on the historical median ratio of pre/post volume. 

**water\_year\_ss\_forecast2.py:** takes in retrospective data and outputs graphs of forecasts from day 30, 60, etc. for each water year, but this time the forecast is until the end of the water year, not only 90 days. The forecast in this case is scaled by the historical median ratio and also the shape is stretched to match the median shape of the 5 closest analog shapes. 

**water\_year\_90dayforecast.py:** forecasts the following 90 days of each water year (LOYO loop) on day 45, 90, etc. of each year. Scales based on historical ratios and matches the shape to the median of the five closest analog shapes. Records metrics such as RMSE, Bias, and NSE. Plots the forecasts for each year and saves them to an output file, and saves the metrics file as well. ^could be merged with the script above^

**loyo\_viz.py:** takes in the output file of metrics from water\_year\_90dayforecast and visualizes each of the metrics over time and in box plots, saving the plot files to a specified output path

**synthetic\_data\_generate.py:** takes in 1-2 years of real ERA-5 data and generates the rest of the \~80 year window with synthetic data (noise added)

**water\_year\_withvar.py:** takes in retrospective flow data for a river, as well as ERA-5 climate data, and forecasts day 30, 60, 90 etc. of water year. Computes rolling 7-day average of climate variables (precipitation, snowpack, etc) and uses a linear regression tool to correlate these rolling averages with the 90-day ahead cumulative volume, finally giving a forecasted 90 day cum volume. Then it uses 50/50 slope and climate features to pick analog shapes and normalize/average them to give the shape of the forecast curve. Then computes the metrics, plots the curves for each day in each water year, saves to a directory, saves the metrics in a csv to the same directory.
